content.thinking:
My generator wrote raw 32-hex-digit strings as addresses — invalid IPv6 text. In mkscale I should use proper IPv6 text (str(ipaddress.IPv6Address(...))). But for the scale test I want to also test the 32-digit colon form... let me just use str(IPv6Address).

Note this is the generator's problem, not the compiler's. Let me fix.

Also note that this exercises the invalid path — good, the compiler correctly rejects invalid address text.

Let me also add a "raw hex digits without colons" invalid test to my invalid fuzz.

s=open('tmp/mkscale.py').read()
s=s.replace('rows.append(["%032x/%d"%(start,length),hop]); hop+=1',
            'rows.append([str(ipaddress.IPv6Address(start))+"/%d"%length,hop]); hop+=1')
s=s.replace('''        rows=[["::/0", 0]]''','''        rows=[["::/0", 0]]''')
s=s.replace('"addresses":["%032x"%rng.getrandbits(128) for _ in range(64)]',
            '"addresses":[str(ipaddress.IPv6Address(rng.getrandbits(128))) for _ in range(64)]')
s=s.replace('rows.append(["%032x/128"%p, i+1])','rows.append([str(ipaddress.IPv6Address(p))+"/128", i+1])')
open('tmp/mkscale.py','w').write(s)
